title: Choose the access route first: public university (homologación + UNEDasiss + PCE) or private university (own test)
duration_realistic: 1-2 counselling sessions, but it must happen 12 months before the intake
what_happens: Spain has two completely different undergraduate access systems and the choice sets the entire calendar. For a PUBLIC university an Indian Std XII student must (a) apply for homologación of the Std XII qualification to the Spanish Título de Bachiller at the Ministerio de Educación, Formación Profesional y Deportes, and (b) buy a UNEDasiss accreditation from UNED that converts the marks to the Spanish 0-10 scale and adds PCE (Pruebas de Competencias Específicas) exam scores. For a PRIVATE university (IE, ESADE, Universidad de Navarra, IQS and La Salle at Universitat Ramon Llull, UIC, CEU) admission is decided by the university's own test, essays and interview, and the homologación paperwork is only needed to complete enrolment - typically by 31 October of the starting year. The public route is grade-ranked and closes in early July; the private route runs in rolling rounds from the previous October.
the_trap: Counsellors treat Spain like the UK and start in the spring. The public route needs the homologación file open roughly 9-12 months before the September intake, because the accreditation and PCE registration both depend on it. Choosing 'we'll decide later' effectively chooses the private route by default.
exact_quote: El sistema de admisión es diferente para universidades públicas y universidades privadas.

title: Assemble, apostille and sworn-translate the school record for homologación (Std X, XI and XII)
duration_realistic: 4-8 weeks in India (board attestation, MEA apostille, sworn translation)
what_happens: Homologación to the Título de Bachiller requires the official Std XII certificate/diploma plus certified mark sheets for at least the last three school years - Std X, XI and XII. India is a Hague Apostille country, so a single MEA apostille is enough; no chain diplomatic legalisation. Every document not issued in Spanish needs an official translation (traductor jurado registered in Spain, a Spanish consulate, or an official translator abroad whose signature is legalised). Verified copies (copias verificadas) are made at a Spanish registry after the originals are apostilled - not before.
the_trap: Students who moved boards or skipped a year cannot produce a continuous three-year record and the file is rejected outright. The other classic failure is translating first and apostilling second - the Ministry requires the copy to be made after the originals are legalised, so the whole set has to be redone.
exact_quote: Homologación a Título de Bachiller: al menos los 3 últimos cursos

title: File the homologación application and collect the volante de inscripción condicional
duration_realistic: 1-2 weeks to file; the volante is issued on filing
what_happens: The application (solicitud de homologación al título de Bachiller) is filed with proof of payment of tasa 079, model 790. It can be lodged at the Ministry's registry in Madrid, at any Delegación/Subdelegación del Gobierno, at the education authority of Cataluña, País Vasco or Galicia if the student will live there, or - crucially for students still in India or the UAE - at the registry of a Spanish diplomatic mission. Paying from abroad is done by bank transfer to the Tesoro Público restricted account at the Banco de España (IBAN ES27 9000 0001 2002 5310 8018, BIC ESPBESMMXXX). Filing produces the volante de inscripción condicional, the receipt that lets the student proceed with UNEDasiss, preinscripción and enrolment while the homologación is still pending.
the_trap: Waiting for the credencial before doing anything else. The volante is the document that unlocks the rest of the chain, and it exists from day one - but only if the file is actually lodged at a registry, not merely prepared. The Ministry's own information pages do not publish the euro amount of tasa 079; get the current figure from the 790 form before transferring, because an insufficient payment sends the file back for subsanación and restarts the clock.
exact_quote: Registros Generales de las representaciones diplomáticas de España en el extranjero.

title: Wait out the homologación decision - the single biggest scheduling risk in the Spanish chain
duration_realistic: Legal limit 3 months; in practice commonly 4-8 months, and longer if documents are queried
what_happens: The Ministry's stated resolution period is three months counted from the date the file is complete, not from the date it was lodged - any request for missing documents resets that starting point. Failure to resolve in time has negative (desestimatorio) effect, which only opens the door to an appeal; the Administration still has to issue an express decision later. Until the credencial arrives the UNEDasiss accreditation stays provisional and university enrolment stays conditional.
the_trap: This step has no accelerator and no escalation path, and it is the reason Spain fails for Indian students who start in March. Build the calendar so that the homologación is filed by November/December for a September start; if the credencial is still pending in the autumn it must reach UNEDasiss by 31 October to change the admission grade for that cycle.
exact_quote: El plazo para la resolución de los expedientes de homologación o convalidación es de 3 meses, a contar desde la fecha en que el expediente se encuentre correctamente cumplimentado.

title: Check each target university's admission criteria before buying UNEDasiss services
duration_realistic: 1-2 weeks
what_happens: UNEDasiss sells separate services and the university decides which ones count: Calificación de Acceso (70 EUR), PCE exams (35 EUR for 1 subject up to 140 EUR for 6), Modalidad de Bachillerato (25 EUR per modalidad), Acreditación de idiomas (25 EUR per language), plus apertura de expediente 30.30 EUR and tasas de secretaría 15.15 EUR. A typical Indian applicant taking four PCE pays roughly 215-240 EUR. Universities publish tablas de ponderación showing which PCE subjects are weighted up to 0.2 for a given degree; UNEDasiss's Información de Universidades tool lists each university's requirement.
the_trap: Prices are published as an image still labelled 'precios25' on the UNEDasiss site as of 14 September 2026, so treat them as the 2025 schedule and re-check at application. More expensive mistake: fees are non-refundable even if a service is denied or the university turns out not to use it, and services cannot be removed once the application is sent.
exact_quote: Los estudiantes deben abonar los precios correspondientes a todos los servicios de acreditación solicitados, aunque estos resulten denegados por parte de UNEDasiss, tras el estudio de la documentación aportada.

title: Apply for the UNEDasiss accreditation online and upload the volante plus apostilled transcripts
duration_realistic: Application window opens 4 February and closes 1 December each year; processing up to 3 months, usually about 3 weeks
what_happens: The student applies at unedasiss.uned.es, pays, and uploads documents. For non-EU systems the required set is the homologación credencial or, if it has not been issued yet, apostilled copies of the last two pre-university years plus the volante proving the homologación has been started. UNEDasiss then calculates the Nota Media de Bachillerato (5-10) and, when PCE results publish, issues the accreditation with the Calificación de Acceso: (0,2 x NMB + 4) + 0,1 x M1 + 0,1 x M2 + 0,1 x M3 + 0,1 x M4, capped at 10. The accreditation is valid for two years.
the_trap: UNEDasiss advises sending the application at least six weeks before the university preinscription closes, and postal documents from abroad take more than 15 working days to arrive - so a student who applies in May for a July deadline is already late. Also note that without PCE the maximum access grade is only 6.0, which is below the cut-off for almost every competitive public degree.
exact_quote: El plazo para solicitar la acreditación de UNEDasiss on line, se abre el 4 de febrero y se cierra el 1 de diciembre de cada año.

title: Register for PCE exams and solve the 'no exam centre in India' problem
duration_realistic: Registration window ~6 weeks; exams sat in late May or early September
what_happens: There are two PCE sittings a year. For 2026 the May/June registration ran 16 March to 28 April with exams in Spain from 25 to 29 May; the September sitting registered 1-22 July with exams 2-8 September. A maximum of six subjects can be taken per sitting and UNEDasiss recommends at least four for non-EU students. The published list of overseas centres for September 2026 includes Abu Dhabi, Doha, Beijing, Moscow, Tehran, London and a dozen Latin American cities - but no centre anywhere in India. Students in a country with no centre must email secretaria.selectividad@adm.uned.es before 31 March (May/June sitting) or 5 July (September sitting) to ask for an alternative.
the_trap: This is the Spain-specific trap almost no Indian counsellor knows: the student either flies to Abu Dhabi or Doha to sit the exams, or writes to UNED early enough to be given an alternative. Discovering it in April means the May sitting is gone and the September sitting publishes results on 16 September - after term has started. For Pave's UAE-resident families this is an advantage, not a problem: Abu Dhabi is a listed centre.
exact_quote: Si en su país no está habilitado un centro de examen envíe un correo electrónico a secretaria.selectividad@adm.uned.es antes del 31 de marzo para la convocatoria de mayo/junio indicando su problema, para que desde la secretaría de las pruebas vean si es posible darle alguna alternativa.

title: Sit the PCE and get the (provisional) UNEDasiss accreditation
duration_realistic: Exam week plus ~3 weeks to results (22 June limit for the May/June sitting; 16 September for the September sitting)
what_happens: PCE are marked 1-10 with two decimals and 5 is the pass mark; only passes above 5 feed the Calificación de Acceso. The accreditation is issued once results publish and is marked provisional while the homologación is pending. Only PCE taken in the same calendar year count, and never more than four.
the_trap: Students bank PCE scores 'for next year'. They do not carry over - results from previous years are explicitly excluded from the access grade calculation, so a gap-year applicant has to sit the exams again.
exact_quote: En ningún caso se tomarán en cuenta para el cálculo de calificación de acceso, calificaciones obtenidas en pruebas de años anteriores ni más de 4 PCE.

title: Private-university track: apply directly in the autumn rounds (IE, ESADE, Navarra, IQS, La Salle, UIC, CEU)
duration_realistic: Rounds from September to spring; a decision typically lands 3-8 weeks after the file is complete
what_happens: Private universities run their own admissions: application file, own entrance test or SAT/ACT, English (and sometimes Spanish) check, essays and an interview. IE University for the 2027-28 cycle closed its Early Round on 18 September 2026, with Round 1 on 6 November 2026, Round 2 on 15 January 2027 and Round 3 on 5 March 2027, then rolling (https://www.ie.edu/university/admission/access-to-university/freshmen-students/); IE publishes a single rule for the Indian national system, an overall average of at least 80%. ESADE, Universidad de Navarra, IQS and La Salle (Universitat Ramon Llull), UIC Barcelona and CEU are rolling or run their own test calendars. But every one of them lists the same legal-access document at ENROLMENT: for non-EU education systems, the homologación certificate from the Spanish Ministry of Education or, in Catalonia, the Generalitat.
the_trap: Counsellors assume 'private = no homologación'. Wrong: the private universities skip homologación for ADMISSION, not for ENROLMENT. The gain is roughly six months of calendar - an offer in November instead of a place allocation in July - which is what makes the visa timeline comfortable.
exact_quote: Educational systems outside the EU: Certificate of equivalence of studies homologation (from the Spanish Ministry of Education or Generalitat de Catalunya).

title: Public-university track in Madrid: preinscripción through the Distrito Único
duration_realistic: A single online application window in June/early July; results ~2 weeks later
what_happens: The six Madrid public universities (Alcalá, Autónoma, Carlos III, Complutense, Politécnica, Rey Juan Carlos) share one application listing degrees in order of preference. In the 2026-27 cycle the general window ran 5-26 June 2026, extended to 6 July 2026 at 14:00 for students from foreign education systems (SEEx); admitted lists published 10 July 2026 at 09:00; an extraordinary phase ran 20-24 July with results on 3 September. The 2027-28 calendar was not published as of 14 September 2026 - use these dates as the shape, not the fact.
the_trap: The Distrito Único calendar states explicitly that students holding homologación of the school-leaving qualification WITHOUT a passed PCE cannot apply in the ordinary phase at all. An Indian student who skips the PCE is therefore pushed to the extraordinary phase in late July, competing only for leftover places.
exact_quote: Estudiantes procedentes de sistemas educativos extranjeros (SEEx): 5 de junio-6 de julio 2026 (hasta las 14 horas).

title: Public-university track in Catalonia: the volante is NOT enough for the June call
duration_realistic: June call 2-26 June; first place allocation 10 July; September call for everyone else
what_happens: Catalonia runs its own preinscripció through the Oficina d'Accés a la Universitat. To enter the June call a non-EU-system student must hold the FINAL homologación credential and have passed PAU/EBAU or the UNEDasiss PCE. With only a volante d'inscripció condicional the student can apply only in the September call, and is placed at the very end of the allocation queue. Catalonia's access grade formula also differs from the UNED one: (0,4 x average of the four compulsory subjects) + (0,6 x the Bachillerato average shown on the homologación credential).
the_trap: This is the sharpest Madrid-versus-Barcelona divergence and it is invisible unless you read the Catalan page. If the family is set on UAB, UB or UPC, the homologación must be RESOLVED - not merely filed - before June, which pushes the start of the file back to roughly November of the previous year. Residents of Catalonia file the homologación with the Departament d'Educació, not the national Ministry.
exact_quote: Disposar de l’homologació definitiva del títol de batxillerat (no hi podràs accedir amb el volant d’inscripció condicional).

title: Submit the preinscripción even if the UNEDasiss accreditation is still unresolved
duration_realistic: Same day; then documents can be topped up until 31 July
what_happens: UNEDasiss tells students to apply within the university deadline regardless of whether the accreditation has issued, attaching the resguardo that proves it was requested. For the 2026-27 cycle the national deadline for international students to apply to public universities was 7 July 2026, with additional documents accepted until 31 July 2026. The universities can verify the accreditation directly on the UNEDasiss platform, so no paid official certificate is normally needed.
the_trap: Students hold back the application waiting for paperwork and miss the window entirely. The window does not reopen. Note the small mismatch worth diarising: UNEDasiss publishes 7 July as the national limit while Madrid's Distrito Único calendar says 6 July at 14:00 - work to the earlier one.
exact_quote: La fecha límite para solicitar la admisión en las universidades públicas por parte de los estudiantes internacionales que deseen iniciar estudios en el curso 2026/2027 es el 7 de julio de 2026.

title: Enrol (matrícula) - provisional until the homologación paperwork lands, with a hard 31 October cut-off
duration_realistic: Days once a place is allocated; the condition runs until 31 October
what_happens: Both public and private universities enrol non-EU-system students provisionally against the volante de inscripción condicional, conditioned on producing the homologación credencial. Universidad de Navarra, for example, makes enrolment provisional and conditional on uploading the volante by 31 October. The same 31 October date is UNEDasiss's limit for receiving a late credencial or outstanding legalised transcripts if the admission grade is to be recalculated for that cycle.
the_trap: 31 October is the real deadline behind the whole chain and it sits six weeks AFTER term starts, which lulls families into thinking there is slack. If the homologación has not been filed by then, the enrolment is void and the student has attended classes that will not be recognised.
exact_quote: Si no dispones del volante de solicitud de Bachiller, tu matrícula será provisional y estará condicionada a que lo aportes antes del 31 de octubre.

title: Pay the matrícula and get the two money documents the visa file needs
duration_realistic: 1-3 weeks from offer to receipts
what_happens: The consulate needs TWO separate documents, not one: proof of admission to the programme showing start date, end date and total cost, AND proof that the enrolment or tuition fee has actually been paid. This mirrors the Reglamento, which requires the applicant to have 'abonado los derechos de inscripción, matrícula o documento equivalente'. Public-university fees for non-EU non-resident students are set per credit and are several times the EU rate - at UC3M, for example, EUR 113.71 per credit for non-EU students against EUR 16.92 for the EU rate, so about EUR 6,800 versus EUR 1,015 for a 60-ECTS year.
the_trap: An admission letter alone is not enough and the file will be held for subsanación, which quietly burns the one-month decision clock. On the public route the place is only allocated in mid-July, so the deposit, the receipt and the visa appointment all have to happen inside two or three weeks.
exact_quote: En el caso de los estudios superiores: tener más de 17 años y haber sido admitido por una institución o un centro de enseñanza superior reconocido para cursar un programa de estudios a tiempo completo que conduzca a la obtención de un título de educación superior reconocido, habiendo abonado los derechos de inscripción o matriculación.

title: Prove financial means at 100% of IPREM per month - EUR 600/month in 2026
duration_realistic: 2-4 weeks to gather sponsor documents and six months of stamped bank statements
what_happens: The legal test is 100% of the IPREM per month for the student, plus 75% for the first accompanying family member and 50% for each additional one. The IPREM is still fixed by Ley 31/2022 (the 2023 State Budget) because the Budget has been rolled over: as published by the SEPE for 2026 it is EUR 600.00 per month and EUR 7,200.00 per year. The Mumbai consulate's own study-visa checklist spells this out as EUR 600 per month for the applicant, EUR 450 for the first family member and EUR 300 for each additional one. For an Indian applicant the consulate expects a signed sponsorship letter, a copy of the sponsor's passport where available, the sponsor's PAN card, and original bank statements for the last six months signed and stamped by the bank. If accommodation is demonstrably pre-paid for the whole stay, that amount is deducted. Money earmarked for tuition does not count towards this test.
the_trap: Two live discrepancies to handle. First, the consulate checklist is still labelled 'In 2025' as of 14 September 2026 - the amount is unchanged at EUR 600 because the IPREM is frozen, but re-check before filing, because it is revised whenever a new Budget passes. Second, families present a lump sum equal to one year's costs but no six-month statement history, or count the tuition they have just paid towards the maintenance figure. Both get refused.
exact_quote: Del indicador público de renta de efectos múltiples (IPREM) fijado en: Ley 31/2022, de 23 de diciembre, de Presupuestos Generales del Estado para el año 2023. … IPREM MENSUAL 600,00 € ANUAL 7.200,00 €

title: Buy health insurance from an insurer authorised to operate in Spain
duration_realistic: 2-5 days
what_happens: The policy must be public or private cover taken out with an insurance entity authorised to operate in Spain, with benefits comparable to the basic common portfolio of the Spanish National Health System, and valid for the whole authorised stay. Practically this means a Spanish-market student policy (Sanitas, Adeslas, Asisa, DKV, Mapfre and similar) with no co-payments, no waiting periods and no repatriation-only cover.
the_trap: An Indian travel-medical or global-student policy is the most common refusal reason on an otherwise clean file, because the insurer is not authorised in Spain and the policy carries copays or exclusions. Buy the Spanish policy before the appointment, not after a refusal.
exact_quote: Contar con un seguro de enfermedad concertado con una Entidad aseguradora autorizada para operar en España, con prestaciones similares a las concedidas por la cartera común básica de servicios asistenciales del Sistema Nacional de Salud.

title: Get the Police Clearance Certificate from the Regional Passport Office, apostilled and sworn-translated
duration_realistic: 3-6 weeks end to end in India
what_happens: Any applicant of legal age whose stay exceeds 180 days must file criminal-record certificates from every country of residence over the last five years. The Mumbai consulate is explicit for India: the PCC must be issued by the Regional Passport Office, apostilled by the Ministry of External Affairs, and submitted with an official (sworn) translation into Spanish. The certificate is valid for six months.
the_trap: A local police-station certificate or a passport-Seva PCC without the MEA apostille is rejected, and the re-issue cycle costs 3-4 weeks. A UAE-resident Indian student needs the certificate from the UAE too, not only from India, because the rule is 'countries of residence in the last five years'.
exact_quote: In case of India, the Police Clearance Certificate (PCC) must be issued by the Regional Passport Office and apostilled by the Ministry of External Affairs, India.

title: Obtain the medical certificate under the 2005 International Health Regulations
duration_realistic: 1-3 weeks including apostille and sworn translation
what_happens: For stays over 180 days the applicant files a certificate from a licensed medical practitioner stating they do not suffer from any disease with serious public-health repercussions under the International Health Regulations 2005. In India it must be apostilled by the Ministry of External Affairs and accompanied by an official sworn translation into Spanish. It is valid for six months.
the_trap: Doctors write a general fitness certificate. The wording has to track the IHR 2005 formula or the consulate returns it. Get the exact sentence to the doctor in advance and have the apostille and translation booked before the certificate is even signed - the six-month validity means it cannot be done too early either.
exact_quote: It must be apostilled by the Ministry of External Affairs, India and submitted together with official (sworn) translation in Spanish.

title: Book the BLS appointment and lodge the type D study visa at least two months before the course starts
duration_realistic: Appointment wait varies by centre and season; the filing itself is one visit
what_happens: Applications go to a BLS International Visa Application Centre by prior appointment; New Delhi covers the northern and eastern states plus Bhutan, Maldives, Nepal and Sri Lanka, Mumbai covers the western and southern states. The applicant must have lived in the jurisdiction for at least six months. The rule is to apply at least two months before studies begin. On fees: the Mumbai consulate's published tariff (3rd quarter 2025) shows the general visa line at INR 8,920 plus an INR 1,675 BLS externalisation charge, while BLS currently publishes INR 9,599 for Indian citizens plus an INR 1,802 service charge - confirm the amount at booking. Reciprocity rates apply only to nationals of Australia, Bangladesh, Canada, the USA and the UK, not to Indian nationals.
the_trap: On the public-university route the two-month rule collides with reality: places are allocated around 10 July for a mid-September start, leaving barely nine weeks. Book the BLS slot the day the place is allocated. Also note the six-month residence rule - an Indian student already studying or working abroad must apply from that country, not from India.
exact_quote: Plazo para solicitar el visado: el visado se debe solicitar con dos meses de antelación al inicio de los estudios o formación, salvo que se acrediten causas justificadas que impidan la presentación con dicha antelación.

title: Wait for the decision - one month by law, longer if an interview or extra documents are requested
duration_realistic: Legal maximum 1 month from the day after filing; plan on 3-6 weeks
what_happens: The consulate has one month from the day after submission to notify the decision; silence means refusal by administrative silence. The period stretches if the office calls the applicant for an interview or asks for additional documents. An approved visa must be collected within two months of notification or the file is archived as abandoned. If the stay exceeds 180 days the visa is valid for a maximum of 365 days of stay and the TIE replaces it thereafter.
the_trap: Families book flights against the visa appointment date rather than the collection date. Also: a refusal has a one-month window for a recurso de reposición to the same consular office - after that the only route is the Tribunal Superior de Justicia de Madrid within two months, which will never resolve in time for the intake.
exact_quote: Plazo de resolución y expedición del visado: el plazo máximo para notificar la resolución es de un mes contado a partir del día siguiente al de la fecha de presentación de la solicitud en la Oficina Consular competente para su tramitación.

title: Understand what the 2025 Reglamento gave you: a permit for the whole degree, not an annual renewal
duration_realistic: Applies from entry; the authorisation runs the official length of the programme
what_happens: Real Decreto 1155/2024 replaced RD 557/2011 and came into force on 20 May 2025. The student route is now an 'autorización de estancia de larga duración por estudios' governed by articles 52-59. For higher education the authorisation lasts the official duration of the studies - so a four-year Grado gets a four-year permit instead of yearly renewals. Its validity starts one month before classes begin and runs fifteen days past the end of studies. Where it is granted for more than a year the student must upload proof of re-enrolment at the start of each academic year to keep it alive. Related changes: the minimum age for a higher-education permit is now 17, not 18; up to two prórrogas are allowed; and RD 316/2026 (in force 16 April 2026) clarified that until the Registro de Instituciones y Centros de Enseñanza Superior exists, 'higher education institution' means one with official recognition from a public administration.
the_trap: Counsellors are still quoting the old annual-renewal regime and budgeting renewal fees and appointments that no longer apply - and, worse, missing the new annual re-enrolment upload, which is now the thing that keeps a multi-year permit valid. The RD 316/2026 clarification also matters for business schools: a programme at a centre without official public recognition may not support a student permit at all.
exact_quote: La duración de la autorización será igual a la de los estudios, programa de movilidad, servicio de voluntariado o actividad formativa, con el límite de un año, salvo en el caso de los estudios superiores previstos en el apartado 1.a) del artículo 52, en cuyo caso la vigencia de la autorización coincidirá con la duración oficial de los estudios.

title: Apply for the TIE within one month of entering Spain
duration_realistic: Appointment within days to weeks depending on the province; card issued in 3-6 weeks
what_happens: Where the stay exceeds six months the student must apply in person for the Tarjeta de Identidad de Extranjero at the Comisaría de Policía or Oficina de Extranjería of the province where the authorisation was processed, within one month of entering Spain. The file needs form EX-17, passport and visa, photographs, proof of address, and the tasa modelo 790 código 012 generated at sede.policia.gob.es. Appointments are booked through the Cita Previa de Extranjería system on the sede electrónica.
the_trap: Cita previa slots in Madrid and Barcelona in September and October are the bottleneck of the whole arrival phase - students routinely cannot find one inside the month. Book the appointment from India before flying if the province allows it, and keep the screenshot: holding a booked appointment beyond the deadline is what protects the student. The official information pages do not publish the euro amount of the 790-012 fee; it is generated on the form itself, so do not pre-pay a figure found on a blog.
exact_quote: En el supuesto de que la estancia por estudios tenga una duración superior a seis meses, la persona extranjera en el plazo de un mes desde la entrada en España deberá solicitar, personalmente, la tarjeta de identidad de extranjero en la Comisaría de Policía o servicios policiales competentes de su lugar de residencia.

title: Register on the padrón municipal (empadronamiento) at the town hall
duration_realistic: Same-day to 3 weeks depending on the city's appointment queue
what_happens: Registration on the municipal padrón is a legal obligation for everyone living in Spain, filed at the ayuntamiento of the municipality where the student habitually lives, with passport and proof of address (rental contract, or a signed authorisation plus documents from the person the student lives with). The certificado de empadronamiento is then needed for the regional health card, bank account paperwork, university admin and many later immigration steps.
the_trap: Landlords of shared student flats refuse to allow empadronamiento, and students then cannot produce the certificate when it is needed. Make the right to empadronarse a condition of signing the lease, and do it in the first fortnight - several cities require an appointment booked weeks ahead.
exact_quote: Toda persona que viva en España está obligada a inscribirse en el Padrón del municipio en el que resida habitualmente.

title: Work rights: up to 30 hours a week, automatically, inside the same comunidad autónoma
duration_realistic: Immediate from the start of the authorisation
what_happens: Under article 57 of RD 1155/2024 a higher-education student permit authorises employed and self-employed work automatically, with no separate work-authorisation application, as long as the work is compatible with the studies. The cap is thirty hours a week. Curricular internships forming part of the study plan need no extra permit at all. The authorisation is geographically limited to the comunidad autónoma that granted it, with an allowance for bordering localities.
the_trap: Breaching the thirty-hour limit is an express ground for extinción of the authorisation, not a warning - a student working full-time over the summer on the same contract can lose their status. The regional limit also catches students who study in Madrid and take a job in Valencia or Seville.
exact_quote: Con carácter general, la actividad laboral a la que se refiere el apartado primero del presente artículo no podrá ser superior a las treinta horas semanales, salvo en el caso de la formación profesional de régimen intensivo que se estará a lo que determine la legislación sectorial.

title: Close the homologación loop and keep the permit alive year on year
duration_realistic: Ongoing; the annual re-enrolment proof is due at the start of each course
what_happens: Two parallel obligations run through the degree. Academically, the credencial de homologación must reach the university and UNEDasiss - 31 October of the starting year is the operative deadline for the admission grade to be recalculated and for provisional enrolment to become firm. Immigration-wise, where the permit was granted for more than a year the student or the institution must file proof of re-enrolment and fee payment at the start of each academic year, and the Administration can ask at any time for evidence that the requirements still hold. Prórrogas are requested electronically in the two months before, or three months after, expiry, and up to two are allowed.
the_trap: Students treat the credencial as paperwork that can drift once term has started. It cannot: after 31 October UNEDasiss will not change the admission grade for that cycle, and a provisional enrolment that never firms up produces a year of credits that do not exist. On the immigration side, forgetting the annual re-enrolment upload is the quiet way to lose a four-year permit in year two.
exact_quote: Los estudiantes que remitan esta documentación pendiente o la credencial de homologación con fecha límite el 31 de octubre, podrán obtener una nueva acreditación con la calificación de admisión modificada si procede La documentación recibida con posterioridad a esa fecha, no modificará la calificación de admisión en esa convocatoria.

title: After graduation: the job-search or start-up residence route
duration_realistic: Apply while the study permit is still valid
what_happens: Students who complete studies at a higher-education institution at EQF level 6 or above (a Spanish Grado qualifies) can move to the residence authorisation for job-seeking or starting a business under the seventeenth additional provision of Ley 14/2013. Alternatively the student can switch to a residence-and-work authorisation; where the person has not held a residence authorisation for at least a year, the new permit is granted for one year and counts as an initial work-and-residence authorisation.
the_trap: This is a selling point families ask about and counsellors get wrong. The route is available on graduating from a recognised institution at EQF 6+, which is another reason the 'is the centre officially recognised' question from RD 316/2026 matters when choosing a private business school. Apply before the study permit lapses - there is no grace period built into the study authorisation beyond the fifteen days after the end of studies.
exact_quote: Las personas extranjeras que hayan finalizado los estudios en un centro o institución de educación superior, alcanzando como mínimo el Nivel 6 de acuerdo con el Marco Europeo de Cualificaciones, podrán acceder a la autorización de residencia al estudiante para la búsqueda de empleo o para emprender un proyecto empresarial conforme a lo dispuesto en la disposición adicional decimoséptima de la Ley 14/2013, de 27 de septiembre.
